title: I Took the Vet Waitlist Policy to the Owner Who Cut the Line

parts.text: I sat on the floor at 7:50 a.m. with a sick terrier because the site said emergency waitlist, first come. A woman in tennis whites walked in at 8:10, hugged the owner-vet, and went straight to an exam room. I was thirty-four. My dog had been throwing up since 4. The clipboard said I was number two. Number one was a cat in a carrier who also did not hug anyone. I photographed the waitlist board and the time. The receptionist whispered, "That's Dr. Pell's sister." Then my dog vomited on the tile they had just mopped for the sister's shoes.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The sister skipped the board; my dog just annotated the mopped tile.

social.video_title: The waitlist hugged its way into an exam room — Part 1/2
social.description: Terrier, 4 a.m. vomit, tennis whites, and a clipboard that thought it mattered. Would you have left?

parts.text: I asked for the emergency policy in writing. It said order of arrival except life-threatening. Tennis whites was a nail trim plus gossip. Dr. Pell came out, saw the tile, and saw the board. They took my dog next. The sister waited with her nail clippers. I paid. I did not yell. I left a review that quoted the policy and the timestamp. The clinic now calls names from the board out loud. My terrier ate rice and recovered. The tile got mopped again, in order.

social.video_title: Nail trim was not life-threatening — Part 2/2
social.description: Written policy, a board that learned to speak, rice diet. Was a hug a triage score?
